name: Atadei / Eastern Atadei
catalog_citation: Krauße, Daniel. 2016. A brief grammar of the Eastern Atadei language of Lembata, Indonesia. Linguistik Indonesia 34(2): 113-128. Open-access PDF, ojs.linguistik-indonesia.org article 45/43.
catalog_locator: p.119 (PHONOLOGY section: vowels/schwa paragraph and syllable-structure table); whole 16-pp paper grepped for stress/accent/tone/penult/prosod
catalog_quote: Vowels are not distinguished by length in Atadei. ... The schwa sound /ə/ can occur word-initially after the inherent glottal stop, in medial position between two consonants or between a vowel and consonant, as well as word-finally in proclitics, such as nĕ ‘he, she, it’. It also occurs in medial position with monosyllabic unstressed words, like tĕk ‘not’. ... Syllables in Atadei are basically CV or CVC, and no word can start with a vowel, as the glottal stop precedes any word-initial vowel. Diphthongs are to be regarded as one vowel (V). The following list illustrates the syllable structure of basic Atadei words: ... CVVC móĕn [ˈmo.ən] ‘yours (sg.)’ CV.CV léma [ˈle.ma] ‘five’ éna [ˈʔe.na] ‘who’ CV.CVC ĕnam [ʔə.ˈnam] ‘six’ ténar [ˈte.nar] ‘boat’ CVC.CV puljua [ˈpul.ɟua̯] ‘twelve’ CV.CV.CV hĕpulò [hə.ˈpu.lɔ] ‘ten’ kikilai [ˈki.ki.lai̯] ‘fingers’ CVC.CVC pultèl [ˈpul.tɛl] ‘thirteen’ kanta…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage and the syllable-structure table are verbatim on p.119 of the held Krauße 2016 text; the paper contains no prose word-stress statement, so 'undetermined / UNSTATED' is a faithful reading. (2) Deciding source: a 2016 16-pp grammar sketch, which is Glottolog's MED and the only description of the languoid anywhere I could verify (Glottolog: 1 descriptive ref; Crossref and Semantic Scholar: nothing else linguistic; Fricke 2019 cites only Krauße 2016 and her own 2015 wordlist for Atadei Painara). open fetches were used instead. (3) fetched sources now: Fricke 2019 (LOT 544, open) gives a prose stress rule only for sister Central Lembata (penult, schwa-penult -> final, heavy-final variation) and is silent on Atadei; Fricke's 2015 Lerek wordlist (LexiRumah, open) gives 588 stress-marked Atadei tokens, 311 penult

sources.quote: No prose statement (wordlist). Primary phonetic transcriptions carry stress marks: by my nucleus count 311 tokens penultimate (ˈtonar, ˈvulan, liˈvunan), 251 final (kəˈləm, vəˈdək with schwa penult; raˈjan, uˈhor, kaˈmak, oˈran with full penult + closed final; also liˈma, maˈta, eˈna V-final), 12 antepenult, 5 earlier (reduplications). I.e. surface stress in this languoid is not uniformly penultimate: schwa penults push stress to the final, and closed finals are very often final-stressed — the same two tendencies Fricke 2019 states in prose for neighbouring Central Lembata, and consistent with

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD). ISBN 978-94-6093-329-5.
sources.quote: For Central Lembata (NOT Atadei): 'the penultimate syllable of the word is stressed, unless the penultimate contains the vowel schwa ... Words with penultimate schwa are stressed at the ultimate syllable, such as /bə.ˈka/'; 'for consonant-final words apparent free variation between penultimate and ultimate stress is found ... [ˈke.dak] ~ [ke.ˈdak] ... tendency to stress heavy final syllables'; trisyllabic stems with final identical-vowel sequences surface with final stress and length ([tuˈluː]). No stress statement is made for Atadei Painara; it is cited only via Krauße 2016 and Fricke's 2015
sources.locator: §3.2.5 'Stress', pp.49-50 (grammar of Central Lembata, sister Central-Lamaholot variety lvu/Kalikasa); §3.8 summary; Atadei Painara mentioned pp.~36, ~130 and in comparative examples only
sources.note: Prose stress rule (pp.49-50) for the closest described sister variety (Central Lembata: penultimate unless schwa penult; heavy-final variation) — useful as a family-level caution note on the record, not as a source for Atadei itself.
